name: Help with energy bills (CEAP)
coverage: Routes Texas households to the local agency that takes utility-assistance applications. The current Texas income guidelines could not be retrieved from the state agency, so this card does not score income and makes no numeric eligibility claim.
limitations: The state income guidelines could not be retrieved, so no income threshold is applied.
This is a referral, not a screen: no label above 'possibly' is produced for this program.
Funding is limited and can run out during a program year; a referral is not a promise of help.
Local agencies differ in what they cover and in how they take applications.
This card does not ask for your county, so it routes you through the statewide referral line rather than naming one office.
eligibilitySummary: The Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program helps Texas households pay heating and cooling bills.
Help is based on income, and the state and the local agency set the rules and the amounts.
Applications are taken by local agencies, which you can find through 2-1-1 Texas.
The local agency makes the final decision, and help depends on funds being available.

evidence.text: LIHEAP, the federal program behind Texas CEAP, helps pay heating or cooling bills and provides emergency help during an energy crisis; eligibility is based on income, and every state and territory sets its own requirements.

The Texas agency pages carrying the current CEAP eligibility rules and income limits returned HTTP 403 on September 19, 2026, from both a direct request and a real browser session, so no Texas income limit is encoded and no numeric screen is offered.
The program pays toward home heating and cooling energy costs, so it applies to a household that is responsible for an energy bill.
The published steps are to check eligibility, find the state or territory office, and apply; some offices accept online applications and others require applying in person.
2-1-1 Texas, run by the Texas Health and Human Services Commission, connects callers to local services and can be reached by dialing 2-1-1 or (877) 541-7905.

Local agencies set their own document lists, so this card asks the agency rather than listing paperwork it cannot verify; bills and proof of income are the usual starting point named by the referral service.
Help is limited by the funds the local agency has available, so a referral does not promise an award or a particular amount.

value.text: The amount depends on your household, your energy costs and the funds the local agency has; no amount is promised here.

documents.label: Ask the local agency what it needs; agencies set their own lists.
Your most recent energy bill, if you have one.

application.label: Find the local agency that takes applications through 2-1-1 Texas (or dial 2-1-1).
Read the federal overview of help with energy bills and how to apply.

fallbackExplanation: We could not read the current Texas income rules for this program, so we are not guessing whether you qualify. The local agency that takes applications can tell you, and 2-1-1 Texas will point you to the one nearest you.
